justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog & Search Container, Cart & Checkout Container and Personalization Engine Container cover R-01, R-02 and R-04. No reviews/ratings component exists despite R-03; Book Reviewer only routes via API Gateway. Search is a controller with no search engine; multi-currency sits in Localization.
justifications.performance_efficiency: AWS ElastiCache (Catalog Caching Component, Redis Cluster), Amazon SQS async processing, CloudFront and latency-based Route 53 routing support targets. Gaps: no autoscaling, no read replicas or search index, and no explicit 3G page-load or 1M MAU sizing.
justifications.compatibility: Third-Party Shipping APIs and Payment Gateway are integrated via HTTPS REST with tokenization and Resilience4j circuit breaker. Standards like OAuth2/JWT are used. Gaps: no anti-corruption adapter for multiple shipping providers, no currency or FX provider, inconsistent shipping paths.
justifications.usability: All four user groups (Book Buyer, Book Reviewer, Store Administrator, Support Agent) reach the API Gateway via HTTPS, and Admin & Support Container serves staff. But the Web Frontend is absent at L2, no reviewer-facing component exists, and localization UX is only a controller.
justifications.reliability: Aurora Multi-Region, Resilience4j circuit breakers, SQS DLQ with 14-day retention, Transactional Outbox, fallback bestsellers and Route 53 routing help. Gaps: no explicit multi-AZ, health checks, autoscaling, backup/RTO/RPO or failover design for the 99.95% target; ElastiCache is single-component.
justifications.security: Strong layered mechanisms: AWS WAF (Security & WAF Component) for OWASP, JWT/OAuth2 validator, TLS 1.3, mTLS in VPC, AES-256 Aurora, KMS-encrypted SQS, Secrets Manager rotation, X-Ray PII redaction, tokenized payments, S3 Object Lock signed Audit Logging Service, GDPR purge.
justifications.maintainability: Domain-aligned containers (Cart & Checkout, Catalog & Search, Personalization, Localization & Compliance) are decoupled via SQS and the API Gateway. Weaknesses: shared Aurora database across services, GDPR logic duplicated in Compliance Manager and Compliance Processing Service, inconsistent L1/L2 naming and tech stacks.
justifications.portability: Containerized on ECS/EKS, with Aurora Multi-Region and the three target regions' latency routing. Heavy AWS-managed coupling (SQS, KMS, API Gateway, Secrets Manager) with no abstraction layer or IaC; Redis and PostgreSQL offer some portability.

sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratio for catalog data
CDN caching of static content unclear
PERF-01.justification: ElastiCache catalog caching, CloudFront and Route 53 latency routing help, but no autoscaling, read replicas or 3G optimisation are specified. 10x load untested.

sensitivity_points: Compute resource contention on shared ECS/EKS
PERF-02.justification: Recomputation is decoupled via SQS, cached profiles and fallback bestsellers, and a separate container. Batch compute isolation is not explicit, and the personalization container has no Aurora link.

sensitivity_points: Queue consumer for deferred shipping not shown
tradeoffs: Eventual shipping consistency versus immediate confirmation
AVAIL-01.justification: Circuit breaker fallbacks, SQS with DLQ and transactional outbox let checkout complete and defer shipping. The shipping retry consumer is not shown explicitly.

tradeoffs: Replication lag versus no lost orders
AVAIL-02.justification: Route 53 latency routing and multi-region Aurora support failover. Compute, cache and SQS regional deployment is unspecified, and Aurora cross-region replication lag may lose orders. Risks unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Pricing logic location split across services
MOD-01.justification: Pricing logic lives in Inventory service and conversion in Localization, so a change touches several components. No dedicated pricing component or configuration mechanism is shown, so changes may exceed pricing and payment.

sensitivity_points: Model format coupling to cache profiles
tradeoffs: Encapsulation versus data schema coupling with telemetry
Verified model loading versus deployment speed
MOD-02.justification: Recommendations are isolated in one container with model loader and a gateway-routed interface, so the algorithm can be swapped locally. Telemetry schema and cache profile formats may couple adjacent components.

SEC-01.justification: AWS WAF gives OWASP Top-10 edge mitigation, with TLS, JWT validation and mTLS. Attack logging is only implied, no input validation or parameterised queries are stated, and there is no reviews component.

sensitivity_points: Deletion consumers not defined across services
tradeoffs: Immutable audit logs versus erasure obligations
SEC-02.justification: Deletion requests are published asynchronously via SQS and audited via S3 Object Lock. No subscribers in Aurora, Redis, SQS or telemetry perform or verify deletion, and the duplicated compliance components blur ownership.
